## Confirmed mechanics
- Boards are rects of 4x4 cells on a 6px pitch. empty=all 1; peg=12px circle

- Click a peg WITH >=1 legal jump -> selects it + marks landings. A peg with
  no legal jump cannot be selected (click = no-op).
- Click a marked landing -> jump: jumper + jumped peg removed, peg appears at
  the landing. 2 actions per jump.
- Jumps are pitch-6 orthogonal, within a board only. Separate boards are NOT
  jump-linked even when a pipe joins them.
- CART = 6x6 frame of 11 around a 4x4 interior of 12, riding the drawn pipe.
  Actions 1/2/3/4 = up/down/left/right, one 6px step along the pipe per
  action; illegal direction = no-op. Arrow moves clear any selection.
  The cart is a normal cell for jumps whenever it is docked 6px from a board
  cell -> it is the ONLY way to move a peg between boards.
- Row 0 = action counter (pixel k = 1). Action 7 (undo) does nothing.
- WIN a level = exactly 1 peg left overall (level_up).
- DEAD END: >1 peg and no jump reachable for ANY cart position -> board
  freezes, pegs turn 2, restart icon appears bottom-left at (51,2); clicking
  it restarts the level. Nothing else responds while frozen.

- `commit` injects ENTRY_GRID = the frame at COMMIT START (not the level entry
  grid); backtest injects the real entry grid. `_erase_cart` restores
  "lane->5 else background" inside the entry-cart footprint, so DO NOT start a
  commit that contains arrow moves while the cart is docked at a board (its
  footprint then covers board pixels and the restore is wrong). Undocked
  start = fine.
- The level_up transition always mispredicts the grid (next level's layout);
  that is unavoidable — put it last in a plan. Scope backtests with
  --level N to check the current level.
